schema.description: Idempotency-Key header. Required: resending the request with the same key returns the automation the first request created, so a lost response never leaves a second schedule running

post.description: Create an automation that runs an agent on a cron schedule. Each run starts a new session in the configured environment and sends the initial events.

description.description: What the automation is for, up to 2048 characters

agent.description: Agent to run in each session. Pass an ID to pin the latest version, or pass an object with type "agent", id, and version to pin a specific version.

environment_id.description: Environment ID each run's session uses

initial_events.description: Initial events sent when each run creates a session. Supply one text user.message event of up to 16384 UTF-16 code units after its text blocks are joined with newlines.

schedule.description: When the automation fires: a cron expression that names a single minute, so it fires at most once per clock hour, read in an IANA time zone name such as America/New_York

repeatArrayField.description: The initial user.message event sent to each session, as JSON, YAML, or @file

examples.command: checkfu automations create --name "Morning report" --agent agent_123 --environment-id env_456 --initial-event '{"type":"user.message","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Write the morning report."}]}' --schedule '{"type":"cron","expression":"0 9 * * 1-5","timezone":"America/New_York"}'

delete.description: Delete a vault and its credentials. A 200 (secrets: erased) means the vault's storage confirmed every secret gone. A 202 (secrets: erasing) means the delete is recorded but that confirmation is still to come; erasure continues in the background. Sessions cannot start new MCP requests using a revoked credential after the change is recorded. custody.erasing counts the credentials whose records have not caught up yet. Sending the delete again returns the current state.

post.description: Archive a vault and its credentials. A 200 means the vault's storage confirmed every secret gone; custody.erasing counts the credentials whose records have not caught up yet. A 202 receipt means the archive is recorded but that confirmation is still to come; erasure continues in the background. Sessions cannot start new MCP requests using a revoked credential after the change is recorded. Resend the archive to check for a 200 confirmation. Reading the vault shows the archived_at timestamp and outstanding credential records.
